steps: Title: picked One Term (label click failed, tapped by coordinates), 2026 era, Ukraine from the globe
Run A: followed every staff pick for 9 months (Gaza vote yes in month 1)
Run B: new game, same nation; first crisis was different (Hostages in Belarus), took the non-staff option; Gaza vote came in month 2 and I voted No, the opposite of A
Compared Israel/Egypt/Saudi reactions to the same vote: clear and plausible
Ran B on staff defaults to month 10 and compared stats with A at the same date
scenarios.notes: The two runs cannot be a clean A/B: crisis order and content differ between games, no seed or replay control. The single like-for-like pair (the Gaza vote) was explained well. A at Aug 2027: approval 45, stability 33, score 81, GDP -14.8%. B at Aug 2027: approval 61, stability 51, score 85. I cannot tell which of my choices caused the gap.

steps: Not played: 1990 Legacy belongs to the other variant

suggestions.what: Restart this exact scenario with the same seed, or rewind to any month, and show a side-by-side of two runs
suggestions.goal_served: replay with a different choice and compare

suggestions.what: After each crisis choice, list the three or four biggest causes of the month's change in each number (the tile and the card disagree today)
suggestions.goal_served: cause and effect in plain terms

suggestions.what: Show the front line / war status of my own war as a plain gauge with a legend and a trend
Make the nation list on the title screen scrollable with a visible window on small laptops
Vary the staff's monthly suggestions and explain why each one is made

delight: Reaction panel after a crisis (Israel 10 to 6, Egypt and Saudi +3) with the opposite vote giving the opposite signs: exactly the cause and effect I wanted (devloop/instances/world-conflict/runs/iter-00/shots/marcus-term/009-m1.png vs devloop/instances/world-conflict/runs/iter-00/shots/marcus-term/057-B2r.png)
Real recent events (the embezzlement scandal around the inner circle, the Hormuz war, an actual Gaza vote) make the 2026 world feel current
Choices list the consequences with arrows before I commit

fun.reason: The decisions are interesting and the news is current, but after a few months I was approving staff defaults.

clarity.reason: Desk layout reads like a briefing; the per-choice consequences are visible. Docked for tile versus card number mismatch and the cryptic front line.

visual.reason: Illustrated scenes are good, a few repeat; I mostly ignored decoration, as expected.

feels_like_a_game.reason: Reads more like a managed briefing than a game, which suits me.

agency.reason: I always knew what to do, but the staff defaults make the best move too easy and my choices matter less than the drift (A lost 19 score points in 9 months doing everything the staff said).

realism.reason: Reactions to the Gaza vote are plausible; Putin repeatedly taking the call about talks every month and a GDP of -15% with approval 45 felt gamey. Not tested on 1960 or 1990.

replay.reason: No seed, no rewind, different openings each game, so I cannot test a what-if cleanly. That is my main use.

recommend.reason: I would show it to my Diplomacy group for the reaction panels, but I would warn them that what-if replay is not there yet.

verbatim: The month-end reactions tell me why things happened, which is rare; but let me rewind and rerun the same month, or it is a toy for what-ifs.
